message.content:
**The Kiss** by Auguste Rodin (1889) is widely regarded as the most iconic and celebrated sculpture of the 19th century. ### Why it stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, a pioneering French sculptor who bridged Romanticism and modernism | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist – a naturalistic rendering of a couple in an intimate embrace | | **Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and human intimacy.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in museums worldwide.
• Its expressive surface texture and dynamic pose exemplify Rodin’s mastery of form and emotion. | | **Legacy** | • The sculpture has been reproduced in bronze, marble, and other media.
• It remains a benchmark for evaluating 19th‑century sculpture and is frequently cited in art history curricula. | ### Other contenders - **The Gates of Hell** (unfinished, 1880–1917) – a monumental bronze group that showcases Rodin’s ambition and thematic depth. - **The Burghers of Calais** (1889) – a powerful civic monument reflecting the social concerns of the era. - **The Thinker** (1902) – technically early 20th century, but often associated with Rodin’s 19th‑century legacy. While several masterpieces share the spotlight, **The Kiss** remains the most universally recognized and celebrated sculpture from the 19th century.
